title: Barn og unges digitale hverdag - i spennet mellom rettigheter, deltakelse, relasjoner og sosiale dynamikk
description: Formålet med forskningsprosjektet er å utvikle kunnskap om mangfoldet av barn og unges digitale hverdagsliv, og hvordan digitaliseringen påvirker deres fellesskap og muligheter for deltakelse i samfunnet. Et sentralt utgangspunkt er å belyse spenningen mellom deres rett til informasjon og deltakelse på nett på den ene siden, og retten til beskyttelse på nett på den andre. Denne spenningen gir opphav til dilemmaer i skjæringspunktet mellom individ og system, hvor hensynet til barns rettigheter må avveies mot behovet for personvern, regulering og kontroll. Videre skal prosjektet utforske dilemma knyttet til hvordan digitale medier inngår i barn og unges sosiale liv – både med jevnaldrende, foresatte, profesjonelle omsorgspersoner, og andre voksne. Digitale samhandlingsformer er integrert i relasjoner og sosiale sammenhenger, og kan bidra både positivt og negativt til tilhørighet, deltakelse og sosial dynamikk – både digitalt og analogt. Prosjektet skal derfor belyse hvorvidt og eventuelt hvordan digital samhandling former barn og unges relasjoner og sosiale dynamikker, og bidra til økt forståelse av disse prosessene og betydningen av dem. Samlet skal oppdraget bidra til økt innsikt i de relasjonelle og samfunnsmessige konsekvensene av en oppvekst der digitale og analoge arenaer er sammenvevd.

title: Prekvalifisering Entreprise 4012 Elektro Somatikk høyhus - Nye Aker
description: Formålet med anskaffelsen er å engasjere en leverandør som skal stå ansvarlig for ytelsene som skal leveres i entreprise 4012 Elektro Somatikk høyhus.Hovedelementene i oppdraget for Entreprisen Elektro Somatikk høyhus er en teknisk totalentreprise som omfatter generell planlegging, prosjektering og design, levering, uttesting, idriftsettelse og dokumentasjon av et komplett og funksjonsdyktig elektrisk anlegg i Somatikk høyhus.

title: Innsatsleder bil
description: Bakgrunn og formål Oppdragsgiver har behov for å fornye kjøretøyet for personell som arbeider med Innsatsledelse i Rogaland brann og redning. Kjøretøyet skal støtte effektiv og sikker innsatsledelse. Anskaffelsen skal bidra til en fremtidsrettet, driftssikker og kostnadseffektiv løsning. Kjøretøyet skal brukes i daglig operativ drift og må støtte sikker transport av personell, verktøy og utstyr. Det er derfor behov for kjøretøy og innrednings løsninger som samlet gir god funksjonalitet, praktisk adkomst, tilfredsstillende ergonomi og forsvarlig håndtering av utstyr i tråd med virksomhetens behov. Beskrivelse av oppdraget Oppdragsgiver skal inngå en kjøpsavtale for levering av 1 stk Innsatslederbil - mellom stor kassebil, ferdig innredet som spesialutrustet kjøretøy til bruk for brannvesenet. Leveransen skal omfatte komplette kjøretøy med tilpasset innredning og nødvendig utrustning for oppdragsgivers bruk. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å gjøre Oppdragsgiver i stand til å ivareta sine pålagte oppgaver innen spesifikke beredskaps- og innsats oppgaver. Dette er et kjøretøy som er i operativ tjeneste drift 24/7. Budsjettrammen for anskaffelsen er kr 1 500 000 eks. mva. Oppdragsgiver forbeholder seg retten til å redusere eller øke anskaffelsens omfang innenfor rammen av det som følger av anskaffelsesregelverket, blant annet som følge av endrede behov, økonomiske rammebetingelser eller organisatoriske forhold. Det etterspørres kjøretøy med egenskaper som gjør det egnet for daglig tjenestebruk, herunder god kapasitet, tilstrekkelig nyttelast med full innredning og fremkommelighet tilpasset varierte driftsforhold. Innrednings løsningen skal være funksjonell for håndtering av innsatsledelse, og samtidig understøtte sikker og ergonomisk bruk i arbeidshverdagen. Nærmere krav til kjøretøy, innredning, ytelse og leveranse fremgår av kravspesifikasjonen. Levering skal skje til Rogaland brann og redning (RBR) i Sandnes.

title: Rammeavtale for service, vedlikehold og rådgivning innen kulde- og varmepumpeteknikk
description: Oslobygg eier og forvalter og drifter et større antall isanlegg i Oslo, porteføljen består av ishaller og utendørs isflater og andre kuldetekniske installasjoner forbundet med Oslobygg KF. Ishallene og isflatene er i hovedsak leid ut til etater og virksomheter i Oslo kommune. Hvilke anlegg som er i drift, vil variere igjennom sesongen og året. Oslobygg KF skal inngå rammeavtale med én leverandør for service og vedlikehold på/av kulde- og varmepumpetekniske anlegg; herunder også rådgivning tilknyttet disse. Oppdragsgivers portefølje på området omfatter isanlegg av varierende grad og størrelse samt også enkelte andre anlegg. . Porteføljen består av blant annet co2-, freon- og amoniakkanlegg. Rammeavtalen skal dekke Oslobygg KF sitt samlede behov for Kulde- og Varmepumpetekniske tjenester i en kontraktsperiode på 4 år.

title: Tolketjenester til Møre og Romsdal fylkeskommune
description: Møre og Romsdal fylkeskommune innbyr til konkurranse for å inngå rammeavtale på levering av tolketjenester. Det skal inngås avtalen med én leverandør. Bakgrunn Møre og Romsdal fylkeskommune har behov for tilgang til kvalifiserte tolketjenester i møte med brukere som ikke behersker norsk tilstrekkelig, eller som har hørselshemminger eller andre kommunikasjonsutfordringer. Behovet omfatter de videregående skolene, karriereveiledningen og tannhelsetjenesten. Tolketjenesten skal bidra til god kvalitet, trygghet og effektiv kommunikasjon mellom ansatte og brukere, og sikre at brukerne får nødvendig informasjon og kan kommunisere om egen helse, opplæring og veiledning på et språk de forstår. Tolking skal også legge til rette for at brukerne kan medvirke aktivt i egen sak. Se for øvrig konkurransegrunnlaget med vedlegg og da spesielt Kravspesifikasjonen (Vedlegg 02) og Oppdragsbeskrivelsen i Bilag 3 i bilaget til rammeavtalen (Vedlegg 08).

title: Rammeavtale for besiktigelse av gategrunn og fasader
description: VAV har behov for å inngå en ny rammeavtale for besiktigelse av gategrunn og fasader. Avtalen vil innbefatte oppsett av rystelsesmålere samt befaring av boliger. Ved flere prosjekter skal det besiktes gategrunn og fasader, både før og etter gjennomføring av prosjekter. Ved slike oppdrag skal det dokumenteres skader påført gategrunn og eiendom, som følge av sprenging, pigging mv. Rystelsesmålere vil i enkelttilfeller settes ut i perioder hvor arbeid pågår. title: 19-UDE-2026 Skole på arbeidsplass
description: Oslo kommune ved Utdanningsetaten og Osloskolen (oppdragsgiver) ønsker å gjennomføre et prosjekt der en gruppe elever får praksisbasert opplæring på en arbeidsplass. I samarbeid med Osloskolen skal leverandøren gi elevene opplæring på arbeidsplass i Vg2 og Vg3 i fag og yrker nevnt over. Målet er at all undervisning og opplæring i vg2/år 2 foregår på arbeidsplass, med forventning om at de fleste deltakerne så skal fortsette som lærlinger i bedriften. title: 26226 Tilbygg og ombygging av Tennfjord barnehage, totalentreprise
description: Konkurransen gjelder totalentreprise for tilbygg og ombygging av Tennfjord barnehage. Bygningskroppen skal forlenges med omtrent 20 meter mot nord for to nye småbarnsavdelinger. Entreprisen omfatter i tillegg en god del ombygginger i det eksisterende bygget. Anskaffelsens verdi anslås til under under EØS terskelverdi. Volumet er et estimat og er ikke bindende for oppdragsgiver. Oppdragsgiver tar forbehold om avlysning av konkurransen, blant annet i forbindelse med budsjettmessig dekning og politisk godkjenning av kommunestyret. Plikten til å stille krav om lærling er vurdert til å gjelde for denne anskaffelsen, jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5h. Se vedlagte seriøsitetsbestemmelser for mer informasjon.

title: Ombygging av Industrivegen 19
description: Herøy kommune ber om tilbod på totalentreprise - ombygging av Industrivegen 19. Delen av bygget som skal rehabiliterast er på ca 385 m2, og er oppført i 3 forskjellige byggetrinn. BT1 oppført i 1985 ca 115 m2, BT2 oppført 1998-2000 ca 95 m2 og BT3 oppført i 2005 ca 175 m2. Prosjektomfang er i hovudsak å totalrehabilitere den innvendige delen i tillegg til mindre endringar av fasade. Totalentreprenør skal også gi ein opsjonspris på nye vindauge, solskjerming type screens og spliteining for kjøling IKT-rom, samt eventuelt frådrag eksisterande inntak/avkast. Detaljert oversikt av arbeidet er å finne i kravspesifikasjonar, sjå vedlegg pkt. 12. Prosjektet skal gjennomførast som totalentreprise og tilbodet skal omfatte komplett arbeid og inkludere prosjektering og leveransar som definert i prosjektets konkurransegrunnlag. Teikningsgrunnlaget er å oppfatte som ei moglegheitsstudiet og TE tar over det totalet ansvaret fram til overleveringstidspunktet. Kontraktarbeida skal ha oppstart direkte etter kontraktsinngåing og prosjektet vert forventa ferdigstilt i løpet av april 2027.

title: Transport- og sorteringslinje for vaskeriet i Helse Bergen HF
description: Helse Bergen HF har behov for å øke kapasiteten og driftssikkerheten i dagens vaskeri. Den eksisterende produksjonslinjen ble installert i 2010 og har over tid vært utsatt for betydelig slitasje. Vaskeriet har høy produksjon og er avhengig av stabil og forutsigbar drift. Det er derfor behov for å fornye og videreutvikle deler av produksjonslinjen, samtidig som eksisterende utstyr som fortsatt fungerer godt, skal kunne inngå i den fremtidige løsningen.

title: Rammeavtale med flere leverandører: Analyse av vitenskapelige prøver 2026
description: NIKU – Norsk institutt for kulturminneforskning, heretter også kalt Oppdragsgiveren, innbyr til åpen tilbudskonkurranse i forbindelse med anskaffelse av Rammeavtale om kjøp av analyse av vitenskapelige prøver fra arkeologiske forvaltningsundersøkelser.Anskaffelsens formål er å inngå kontrakt med én eller flere leverandører som skal utføre konkrete typer analyser av vitenskapelige prøver. Kontrakten er delt opp i flere deler. En leverandør kan gi bud på én, flere, eller alle deler av kontrakten, og hvert deltilbud evalueres uavhengig av en leverandørs andre deltilbud.

title: 26231 Ny konkurranse E1: Bygg og Anlegg, nytt vannverk Dokka
description: Konkurransen gjelder entreprise for oppføring av bygg for nytt vannverk i Dokka. Oppdraget inkluderer VA-infrastruktur. Entreprenøren pålegges koordineringsansvar for sideentreprenør (leverandør av prosess og automasjon) Anskaffelsens verdi anslås til ca. NOK 25.000.000,- . Volumet er et estimat og er ikke bindende for oppdragsgiver. For nærmere informasjon viser vi til anskaffelsesdokumentene. Oppdragsgiver tar forbehold om avlysning av konkurransen, blant annet i forbindelse med budsjettmessig dekning og politisk godkjenning. title: Lastebil med plan og kran til Sandefjord havnevesen
description: Bakgrunn Sandefjord havnevesen har behov for å fornye kjøretøyparken som følge av utskiftingsbehov. Den nye lastebilen skal benyttes løpende til ulike oppdrag over hele kommunen. Bruken innebærer hyppig forflytning mellom arbeidssteder, betydelig kjøring på vei og et driftsmønster der kjøretøyet i stor grad vil være i kontinuerlig bruk. Anskaffelsen skal derfor bidra til en mer robust og pålitelig oppgaveløsning i den daglige driften. Beskrivelse av oppdraget Anskaffelsen omfatter levering av én 2-akslet lastebil med plan og kran til Sandefjord havnevesen. Kjøretøyet skal dekke virksomhetens behov for et funksjonelt og driftssikkert arbeidsredskap til løpende oppdrag på ulike lokasjoner i kommunen. Leveransen skal inkludere komplett kjøretøy med plan og kran, tilpasset den aktuelle bruken, samt innbytte av eksisterende eldre lastebil. Anskaffelsen gjelder en samlet leveranse der nytt kjøretøy og håndtering av innbytte inngår som del av oppdraget.

title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?
description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

title: How can technology enable fast-growing digital public service providers to dynamically scale their service management capabilities as demand, complexity and customer expectations increase?
description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?​
description: With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed. Dialysis journeys account for more than 40% of all non-emergency patient transport activity, costing 9.1 million GBP annually. Yet current arrangements can be inconsistent, creating avoidable pressures for patients, providers and NHS services. NHS Scotland is seeking innovative, patient-centred and sustainable solutions that improve reliability, efficiency and patient outcomes, while reducing administrative burden and delivering better value for money.

Dit Excel bestand kan opgevraagd worden bij de gemeente Oude IJsselstreek door een verzoek hiertoe in te dienen op het e-mailadres aanbesteding@oude-ijsselstreek.nl . title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

Sylinterit uusitaan, vanhat lukkorungot ja helat säilytetään. Urakoitsija on velvollinen tutustumaan kohteisiin omatoimisesti ennen tarjouksen antamista ja varmistamaan lukituskaavioiden ajantasaisuus. Jätekatokset, piharakennukset, postilaatikot yms. lukitukset kuuluvat urakkaan kohteissa, joissa nämä ovat ennestäänkin lukittuja. Urakkaan kuuluu lisäksi lukkojen telkien ja avainpesien (käyttölukot, varmuuslukot, pitkäsalvat) voitelu ja ruuvien kiristys. Muut tarvittavat korjaukset tehdään tarvittaessa lisätyönä. Urakka sisältää kaikki työt ja tarvikkeet valmiin lopputuloksen saavuttamiseksi sekä uuden lukituskaavion. Uuden lukituskaavion lisäksi laaditaan yhteisistä tiloista päivitetyt sijoituspohjapiirrokset tilaajalle. Lukituskaaviot ja uudet avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteisiin (huoltoyhtiö/lukkoliike). Lukostojen laajuus on vanhan lukoston mukainen seuraavin huomautuksin: - avaimia 3 kpl / avaintyypit asunto, lehdenjakaja, reitti, kerhohuone jne. - huoltoavaimia 7 kpl, joista 1kpl toimitetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainsäilöön - yleisavaimia 7 kpl - kaikki avaimet leimataan (yksilöity tunnus) - lukoston käytettävissä olevan reservin tulee olla mahdollisimman laaja Avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteeseen viimeistään 14vrk (2 viikkoa) ennen sovitun asennusajan aloittamista TELETILOJEN SARJOITUS KTL1E Lisäksi kaikkien kiinteistöjen yhteiset teletilat sarjoitetaan KTL1E-järjestelmään ja rakennuksien ulkoseinään asennetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainpesä (mikäli tyhjiä paikkoja ei ole, kuuluu avainsäilöputken seinään poraaminen myös urakkaan). Yhteisiä teletiloja ovat talojakamot, alijakamot, kerrosjakamot ja yhteisiin tiloihin asennetut kytkentäpaikkoja tai telelaitteita sisältävät muut ovelliset kotelot ja rasiat. KTL1E-avainsäilöputkeen toimitetaan 1kpl kohteen huoltoavaimia. Kaksi avainsäilön käyttöavainta toimitetaan muiden avaimien mukana avainhallintapisteeseen. KTL1E järjestelmän liittymismaksuista vastaa tilaaja. Asukkailla on oltava tiedotteen saatuaan vähintään 14 vrk aikaa hakea avaimet avainhallintapisteestä ennen töiden aloittamista. Tiedotteiden jakamisesta vastaa tilaaja. Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/016 - Modular Wind Power For North Operations The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) are seeking innovative solutions to develop modular, stand-alone wind-powered electric generator systems that can be easily transported, deployed, and maintained in remote northern locations to provide reliable, clean energy under extreme cold, high-wind, and icing conditions. Background & Context The demand for electrical power and space heating in the Canadian Subarctic and High Arctic is fulfilled almost exclusively with diesel-fired generators. The DND/CAF is seeking to reduce reliance on fossil fuels for the generation of electrical power in the North to minimize operational, logistical, and environmental burdens. Wind turbines suitable for DND/CAF operations are in limited use in the North, as existing installations tend to fall outside the desired capacity range. While small units that deliver up to 6 kilowatts (kW) have been deployed in some communities, and commercial turbines typically exceed 1 megawatt (MW), there is a critical gap in the 25–100 kW range—an ideal scale for remote DND sites. In addition, northern operating conditions present major technical and environmental hurdles that must be overcome before wind turbines can be fully exploited as a source of alternative energy. Canada's far North and Arctic regions are characterized by seasonally frozen ground, deep snow, rugged terrain, permafrost, and extreme temperatures that can reach –60 degrees Celsius (°C), with frequent high winds of 80–120 kilometers per hour (km/h). Ice rimming of wind turbine blades further threatens performance and efficiency. Innovative approaches are therefore needed to adapt conventional wind-powered electric generator designs to withstand these harsh northern conditions and operate effectively under both low and high wind scenarios. Climate change adds additional complexity, as thawing and refreezing permafrost can cause buildings and foundations to sink, shift, or crack. While not the primary focus of the challenge, consideration must be given to the design of the foundations to keep the turbines level and stable despite seasonal ground movement. There is a need for wind-powered electricity generators that are logistically efficient, easy to deploy, and maintainable in isolated northern locations. Many DND/CAF sites exist in remote areas or within small Arctic communities that have limited or no road access and must be reached by alternative means of transportation such as barges or heavy-lift aircraft. Consequently, new systems must feature modular designs that can be transported and assembled on site with minimal heavy-lift equipment by non-technicians using commonly available tools. To ensure sustained operation, proposed solutions should use readily available parts, be serviceable by local tradespeople, and operate with minimal human intervention once deployed. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Provide a design for a wind-powered electrical generation system in the 25–100 kW range, incorporating details of the structural, mechanical, electrical, and control elements required. • Provide integration and operational demonstration plan(s), showing how the wind-powered electric generator system can function in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold (down to –60 °C), high winds (up to 120 km/h), and icing conditions without intervention. • Integrate with existing electrical power systems or microgrids and must enable coordinated operation with other energy sources and support performance under varying generation and load conditions. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship — ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). • The modular design must enable onsite assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring the wind powered electric generator system can be serviced using standard mechanical and electrical tools, without reliance on specialized proprietary equipment or manufacturer field support. Desired Outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Electromagnetic interference that complies with MIL STD 461G, Department of Defense Interface Standard for the Control of Electromagnetic Interference Characteristics of Subsystems and Equipment. • Foundation design that accounts for Arctic ground conditions, including permafrost, active-layer variation, and freeze-thaw effects, over the intended design life of the generator.

This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/017 - RF Data Fusion for Command and Control The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) are seeking innovative software-based solutions to seamlessly convert, analyze, and fuse real-time, domain-specific, content-rich data transmitted over radio frequency (RF) bearers into a secure, standardized pan-domain Command and Control (C2) format to enhance interoperability and enable timely, data-driven decision-making across all domains and levels of command. Background and context Radio frequency (RF) communications in military operations are inherently bandwidth-constrained and vulnerable to jamming, interference, and environmental effects, making them unreliable in contested environments. To maintain timely and effective support across all warfighting domains, data transmitted over RF bearers should be transformed into compact, structured messages, such as eXtensible Markup Language (XML)-based Message Text Formats (MTF) or other machine-readable schemas. Such messages should be optimized for transmission over tactical networks including Low Frequency (LF), Very Low Frequency (VLF), High Frequency (HF), Ultra High Frequency (UHF), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM). This approach enables resilient, standards-based communication across domains (land, air, maritime, cyber, and space) and functional services (e.g., Joint Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR), medical, logistics), in line with doctrinal requirements for pan-domain operations. CAF tactical messaging remains largely dependent on legacy systems. These systems are inflexible, poorly suited to machine-to-machine exchange, and increasingly misaligned with NATO’s shift toward XML-based, data-centric frameworks. CAF operators currently lack integrated, machine-readable messaging systems. As a result, they must manually convert voice, chat, and text inputs into formal military products including orders, situation reports, and Requests for Information (RFIs) to comply with command structures and coalition standards. Modern, pan-domain operations require that doctrinal and technical Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) be met at the speed of operational relevance, with messaging that is interoperable, standardized, and capable of supporting real-time, data-driven decision-making in joint and coalition environments. As NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, and other Five Eyes partners adopt XML-based, machine-readable messaging frameworks, the CAF is prioritizing alignment with these emerging data models to improve interoperability, operational agility, and mission effectiveness. The DND/CAF are seeking innovative, interoperable, and scalable solutions that will contribute to the development of a next-generation digital military RF messaging and data exchange. Innovators are invited to propose technologies, platforms, or integrated systems. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Be a software-based capability (e.g., standalone application, plug-in, middleware, or service). • Support DND/CAF operations across all domains (land, air, maritime, space, cyber) and functional services (e.g., C2, intelligence, logistics). • Implement structured, standards-compliant messaging (e.g., MTF-XML) and data exchange protocols (e.g., National Information Exchange Model (NIEM), NATO Core Data Framework (NCDF)), with documented interfaces for importing, exporting, and exchanging data using those standards. • Be configurable and modular, supporting Character-Oriented Information Exchange (COIE) processing and designed for future extensibility (e.g., to accommodate emerging or disruptive standards). • Provide documented interfaces and standards-based data exchange mechanisms to support system integration, including use within experimentation, simulation, and wargaming environments. Desired Outcomes The proposed solution should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Operability in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Low Bandwidth (DDIL) environments, with scalability to support evolving mission requirements and force structures. • Enhanced user experience features such as intuitive interfaces, multilingual support, automation of routine workflows, and built-in decision aids. • Standardized, documented integration interfaces (e.g., application programming interfaces (APIs)) to enable integration with at least one Service Management or Service Monitoring tools or platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft System Center, Azure Monitor, etc.). • Readiness for future integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities to support data fusion, intelligent message prioritization, and real-time decision support.

Background and context The CAF’s strategic update Our North, Strong and Free (2024) directs an expansion of military operations in the Canadian North. RTCs deployed in remote Arctic regions must sustain personnel with safe water, sanitation, and waste-handling capabilities while minimizing logistics and environmental risk. In 2023, the IDEaS Pop-Up City contest demonstrated advanced, containerized power-water-waste systems. These prototypes significantly reduced solid-waste mass and potable-water demand but were not tested under Arctic winter conditions. Material brittleness, freezing of fluids, and power-efficiency issues remain key obstacles. This challenge will bridge this gap by developing, and then testing integrated cold-weather water and waste technologies under Arctic winter conditions (e.g., Op NANOOK). The objective of the challenge is to support the development of a proven, deployable, Canadian-made, Arctic-ready water-and-waste system enabling CAF RTCs to operate independently, safely, and sustainably in the North with drastically reduced logistics burden and environmental impact. Essential outcomes Proposed solutions must meet the following requirements: • Integrated capability combining water purification, wastewater treatment and solid-waste reduction suitable for camps of up to 50 personnel. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship – ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20 ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). The modular design must also enable on site assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Treated outputs must meet or exceed Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and Health Canada Drinking-Water Guidelines. • Function continuously in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold down to -40°C. • Resource efficiency must be demonstrated through a reduction in resupply volume and frequency (fuel, water, consumables) by at least 75% from baseline (see Table 1 below). • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring that the solution can be serviced using common trades and tools available to CAF in deployed operations in remote areas. Desired outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Integrated power. • Operable in extreme heat conditions (up to +40°C). • No manual pre-processing of solid waste. • Recovery and reuse of waste-heat or by-products. • Can be scaled to suit camps of over 50 personnel, up to 1500 personnel. Maßnahmen zur Gestaltung von Freianlagen sind nicht Gegenstand der vorliegenden Planung.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Zweiphasiger städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Wettbewerb nach RPW 2013 - Produktives Quartier Gutleut-West
description: Gegenstand des Wettbewerbes ist ein städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Entwurf in dem gezeigt wird, wie die Transformation eines gewerblich geprägten Bestandsareals zu einem nutzungsgemischten, klimaangepassten und gemeinwohlorientierten Quartier gelingen kann. In einer Stadt mit hoher Flächennachfrage und begrenzten innerstädtischen Entwicklungsreserven treffen hier Ansprüche unmittelbar aufeinander, die sich andernorts oft räumlich aus dem Weg gehen: Wohnen und Gewerbe, Logistik und Aufenthalt, soziale Infrastruktur und Produktion, Freiraum und Verdichtung. Die entscheidende Frage lautet deshalb nicht, welche Nutzung sich am Ende durchsetzt. Interessanter ist, wie aus dieser Konkurrenz ein Stück Stadt entstehen kann. Aufgabe des Wettbewerbs ist es, eine eigene räumliche Antwort zu entwickeln. Gesucht wird vornehmlich nicht das möglichst vollständige Bild eines irgendwann „fertigen“ Gutleut-West. Gesucht wird vielmehr ein städtebauliches und freiraumplanerisches Gerüst, das Orientierung gibt, ohne Entwicklung einzuschränken. Es soll durch zu entwickelnde Prinzipien Qualitäten sichern und zugleich Spielräume eröffnen – für unterschiedliche Nutzungen, Träger:innen, Eigentümer:innen und Entwicklungszeitpunkte. Die Ausloberin beabsichtigt, unter Würdigung der Empfehlung des Preisgerichts, das mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichnete Team mit der Ausarbeitung des Wettbewerbsergebnisses zu beauftragen. Die Ausloberin wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb gemäß § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchführen. Dabei behält sich die Ausloberin vor, das Verhandlungsverfahren zunächst nur mit dem mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichneten Team durchzuführen. Scheitern diese Verhandlungen oder besteht ein wichtiger Grund, der einer Beauftragung des 1. Preisträgers entgegensteht, werden die weiteren Preisträger zur Teilnahme an den Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Das Wettbewerbsergebnis wird im anschließenden Vergabeverfahren als Zuschlagskriterium mit 60 % gewichtet. Die Rangfolge der Preisträger gemäß der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts wird dabei entsprechend berücksichtigt, d.h. der 1. Preisträger erhält im Kriterium ‚Wettbewerbsergebnis' die höchste Punktzahl, der 2. Preisträger die zweithöchste usw. Die weitere Bearbeitung umfasst den städtebaulichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 51 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone III, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie den freiräumlichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 52 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone III, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie die Erstellung eines "Qualitätshandbuchs". Eine darüberhinausgehende Beauftragung weiterer Planungsleistungen bleibt vorbehalten und ist nicht Bestandteil dieses Auftragsversprechens. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines Rahmenplans mit integrierter Freiraumplanung als Vorstufe zum Bebauungsplan nach BauGB sowie als Grundlage für das im Anschluss geplante Konzeptverfahren für die hochbauliche Entwicklung auf den Baufeldern. Die Preisträger:innen verpflichten sich, im Falle einer Beauftragung durch die Ausloberin, die weitere Bearbeitung zu übernehmen und durchzuführen. Im Zuge der Überarbeitung der Wettbewerbsergebnisse treten sie mit der Bürgerschaft und Schlüsselpersonen vor Ort im Rahmen von Dialogformaten in Austausch (z.B. Vorstellung des Wettbewerbs-Ergebnisses, Rückfragenbeantwortung, Aufnahme von Hinweisen für weitere Bearbeitung). Die Beauftragung erfolgt vorbehaltlich des Abschlusses des erforderlichen Vergabeverfahrens, der erforderlichen haushaltsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen, der Eignung des Teilnehmers sowie des Vorliegens eines wichtigen Grundes, der einer Beauftragung entgegensteht. Im Falle einer weiteren Bearbeitung werden durch den Wettbewerb bereits erbrachte Leistungen des Preisträgers bis zur Höhe des zuerkannten Preises nicht erneut vergütet, wenn und soweit der Wettbewerbsentwurf in seinen wesentlichen Teilen unverändert der weiteren Bearbeitung zugrunde gelegt wird.

The North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990-Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction which has a small business size standard of $45 Million. Project Scope: The contractor shall repair four shallow slides (Slides 18, 20, 21, and 28) on the upstream and downstream dam embankment slopes. Work includes the removal of slide debris; excavation of the slide area with bench-cutting into the stable embankment and a keyway into the foundation toe; lime-treatment of excavated soil; placement and compaction of treated soil to restore original design contours; and final surface restoration with riprap on the upstream slope and topsoil with vegetation on the downstream slope.
